MYRTLE AVENUE NEGRONI WEEK 2026 (SPONSORED)
Myrtle Avenue Negroni Week 2026
September 21–27
Bitter, Bold & Anything But Ordinary!
Negroni Week returns to Myrtle Avenue September 21–27, with
10 bars and restaurants across Fort Greene and Clinton Hill
putting their own spin on the iconic cocktail. This year, bartenders venture beyond the classic trio of gin, Campari and sweet vermouth with mezcal, cherry, coffee, chocolate, rhubarb, mushrooms, orgeat…and even tomato, basil and olive oil.
Here’s what’s mixing
:
•
Doppelgänger
–
The Triangle In The Square
: A smoky, ruby-red mezcal riff with Cocchi Americano, Averna and rhubarb bitters.
•
The Emerson
–
City-Sangue Cherry Negroni
: A deep-red, cherry-forward blend of Citadelle Jardin d’Été, Campari, sweet vermouth and Luxardo Sangue Morlacco.
•
LaRina Pastificio & Vino
–
Diavolo in Me
: Bright, bittersweet and slightly sour, with gin, Italian bitters, lemon, orgeat—and a little devil in it.
•
Little Falcon
–
House Negroni
: The Italian classic heads in a distinctly French direction, with a touch of French elegance.
•
Lula Mae Sporting Club
–
Three Ways to Negroni
: Choose from Classic, bright and botanical White, or smoky Mezcal.
•
Neno’s
–
El Ahumadito Negroni
: Poblano-infused mezcal gives this one a smoky Mexican spin. Try the
$22 El Ahumadito Experience
, pairing it with a pork belly taco.
•
Osteria Brooklyn
–
Smoked Negroni
: Gray Whale Gin, made with California-sourced botanicals, gives this riff its West Coast character.
•
Putnam’s Pub
–
Wild Rose Negroni
: Featuring Glendalough Wild Rose Gin, made with rose petals from the garden of owner Gerry Rooney’s late mother, Rose.
•
Rosticceria Evelina
–
Five Ways to Negroni
: Five inventive riffs include coffee, chocolate and the savory Negroni Pie with olive oil-washed gin, tomato-infused Campari and basil vermouth.
•
Vine
–
Shroom Negroni
: An earthy, umami-rich riff combining gin, Campari and Carpano Antica with Veda mushroom liqueur and shiitake mushroom syrup, finished with ground shiitake and an edible flower.
Drink for a cause! Each participating venue has also made a donation to
Slow Food
as part of Negroni Week’s global fundraising initiative.
Ten locations. Seven days. Countless ways to Negroni.
Cheers, salute, salud and sláinte
…Negroni Week is back on Myrtle Avenue!

The Mingle Games, Round 02
Meet new people, play fast-paced games, and see where the night takes you at
The Mingle Games
, a social game night of competition, cocktails, and connections!
Check in and an app sends you to your first game station, where you’ll play a quick round with a few strangers. Then it’s on to a new table with new people. You’ll never sit with the same person twice, so there’s no awkward hovering or figuring out who to talk to.
A guest comedian host guides you through the evening, working the room and keeping the competition moving between rounds. If you hit it off with someone, tap to connect in the app. If you both tap to connect, you can exchange contact info after the night. Station winners are entered into a prize drawing!

Title: RIC BURNS AND JAMES SANDERS — “NEW YORK: THE FUTURE OF CITIES”  — REBUILDING LOWER MANHATTAN

Content:
RIC BURNS AND JAMES SANDERS — “NEW YORK: THE FUTURE OF CITIES”  — REBUILDING LOWER MANHATTAN
What does the future of a city look like — and how does its past shape what’s possible?
On Thursday, September 24 at 6 p.m., join the Downtown Alliance and Pace University for a screening of highlights from Ric Burns and James Sanders’ new two-part documentary series:
“New York: The Future of Cities.”
With these episodes, Burns and Sanders continue their original award-winning eight-part, 17-1/2-hour series, “New York: A Documentary Film,” which originally aired on PBS between 1999 and 2003.
TICKETS HERE
The screening will be followed by a conversation with Burns, Sanders and Vishaan Chakrabarti, architect and founder of PAU (Practice for Architecture and Urbanism).
Spanning the first two decades of the 21st century, “The Future of Cities” captures a New York in the midst of remarkable transformation, from the aftermath of September 11 to the city’s emergence as a global “superstar city.” Along the way, the film explores the challenges that cities everywhere now face, including infrastructure, immigration, governance, equity, financial crises, climate change and resilience.
At the heart of this story is Lower Manhattan, a neighborhood whose transformation over the past 25 years has helped shape the trajectory of the city itself. From the rebuilding of the World Trade Center site and the creation of new public spaces to the growth of a vibrant residential, cultural and commercial district, Lower Manhattan has undergone one of the most significant urban transformations in modern New York.
This special evening will take a closer look at how and why Lower Manhattan was rebuilt, the choices and ideas that shaped its transformation and its place in the broader story of New York’s evolution. Through the lens of “The Future of Cities,” the discussion will explore what the rebuilding of Lower Manhattan reveals about New York’s resilience, creativity and capacity to continually reinvent itself.
Ric Burns
, a scholar trustee of the New York Historical, is the founder of Steeplechase Films and an internationally recognized documentary filmmaker co-writer and producer of “The Civil War” and “New York: A Documentary Film.”
Vishaan Chakrabarti
is an architect and founder and creative director of PAU (Practice for Architecture and Urbanism), where he leads the firm’s portfolio of cultural, institutional and public projects, which include the redesign of New York’s Penn Station, designer of the Domino Sugar Refinery and designing the FAA’s sustainable air traffic control tower prototype. Chakrabarti has over 30 years of urban architecture experience, including president of Moynihan Station Venture at The Related Companies and director of the New York Department of City Planning’s Manhattan office. He has also been dean of University of California, Berkeley’s College of Environmental Design and a professor at Columbia University’s architecture school. Chakrabarti is the author of “A Country of Cities: A Manifesto for an Urban America” and “The Architecture of Urbanity: Designing for Nature, Culture, and Joy.” In 2025, he was awarded the Edmund N. Bacon Urban Design Award.
James Sanders, FAIA
, is the architect behind the design and research firm James Sanders Studio, as well as an author and filmmaker. With Ric Burns, he wrote and produced “New York: A Documentary Film,” and its companion book, “New York: An Illustrated History.”

Title: THE KLEZMATICS & FRIENDS 40TH ANNIVERSARY CONCERT (SPONSORED)

Content:
THE KLEZMATICS & FRIENDS 40TH ANNIVERSARY CONCERT (SPONSORED)
For four decades, these GRAMMY-winning trailblazers have redefined Yiddish music for new generations, blending deep tradition with fearless creativity and a spirit of joy, resilience, and social change. Join us for a one-night-only celebration featuring special guests, longtime collaborators, and music spanning their remarkable 40-year journey of radical joy with a legacy unlike any other in contemporary roots music.
The evening will feature music from all of The Klezmatics’ fourteen recordings, including their GRAMMY Award-winning album,
Wonder Wheel
with lyrics by Woody Guthrie, with a special focus on Woody Guthrie’s inspiring texts, and The Klezmatics’ collaborations with Guthrie.
Special guests include Janis Ian, Lavender Light Gospel Choir, Susan McKeown, Danny Blume, and more!
The Klezmatics & Friends: Celebrating 40 Years of Radical Joy
Thursday, September 24 at 7pm
Symphony Space
2537 Broadway & 95th Street, NY, NY 10025

Title: TARGET MARGIN THEATER PRESENTS THE NONSENSE LAB STARTING SEPTEMBER 17 (SPONSORED)

Content:
TARGET MARGIN THEATER PRESENTS THE NONSENSE LAB STARTING SEPTEMBER 17 (SPONSORED)
The NONSENSE LAB
will offer three productions, each for 6 performances, from September 17 to October 3, 2026, in The Doxsee, and three 1-time events (talks, installations and performances). All of our Lab Artists start with these questions: how can we work meaningfully with the nonsense around us? How can we create poetry and beauty through nonsense itself? Lead Artists examine the nonsensical world around us while grappling with themes of humanity, isolation, and memories through music, dance, performance, puppetry, and toy theater.
This season our Labs are led by three Artists from diverse disciplines. Choreographer
Caroline Fermin’s
Let Me Be an Animal
is an evening-length dance celebrating the slow, awkward, sweaty, and questioning parts of ourselves. Associate A.D.
Adam M. Kassim
creates an explosion of politics, pop culture, and history in
We’ll Jump Off That Bridge When We Get There
; Toy theater creator / puppeteer
Kathleen Kennedy Tobin
builds a tiny cruel nonsense universe called
The Charnel House
.
One-time music and artistic events enrich the program. On Tuesday, September 22,
TMT Community Café for the Nonsensical
will feature a collective reading of
Entertainer Zero Machine: A Cyber Peep Show Lyric of Illegitimate Theater
by Ron Allen. Saskia Lane leads an evening of nonsense music in
Nothing to See Here
on Monday, September 28 and
Theresa Buchheister
serves up an evening of impossibility, delight and challenge in
Uh Oh Manifest(o)ing
on Wednesday, September 30. Both Saskia and Theresa will curate a gathering of artists to offer a confetti cannon of nonsense in all its artistic forms.
The Nonsense Lab
runs September 17 through October 3 at the Doxsee Theater in Sunset Park, Brooklyn.
Tickets starting from $20:
TargetMargin.org/NonsenseLab
